q: A process of making a magnetic material into a magnet is called _____.
e: Magnetisation is the specific term for the process of converting a magnetic material into a magnet.

q: Two types of magnetisation are magnetisation by stroking and magnetisation using _____.
e: The two primary methods of magnetisation are the mechanical stroking method and the electrical method using direct current.

q: The best way to make powerful magnets is to use the magnetic effect of an _____.
e: Passing an electric current through a solenoid is the most effective method for creating powerful magnets.

q: A steel bar placed inside a solenoid with direct current passed through it becomes a _____.
e: Steel retains its magnetism after the current is switched off, making it a permanent magnet.

q: If an iron bar is placed inside a solenoid with direct current, it becomes magnetised temporarily as a(n) _____.
e: Iron loses its magnetism quickly once the current stops, functioning as a temporary electromagnet.

q: The polarities of the magnet produced by a solenoid depend on the _____ of the electric current.
e: Reversing the direction of the direct current will reverse the $N$-pole and $S$-pole of the resulting magnet.

q: In magnetisation by stroking, the magnet must be lifted _____ above the bar between successive strokes.
e: Lifting the magnet high prevents the return stroke from demagnetising or reversing the alignment of the domains.

q: The end of the steel bar where the strokes finish always has the _____ polarity to that of the end of the stroking magnet in contact with it.
e: The finishing end of the bar acquires the opposite polarity of the stroking magnet's contact end due to magnetic induction.

q: When a piece of unmagnetised magnetic material is brought near to the pole of a permanent magnet, it is attracted and becomes a magnet itself. This is called _____.
e: Induced magnetism is the temporary magnetisation of a material caused by the proximity of a permanent magnet.

q: In induced magnetism, the north pole of the permanent magnet induces a(n) _____ in the near end of the soft iron.
e: Unlike poles attract, so the $N$-pole of the permanent magnet induces an opposite $S$-pole in the nearest end of the soft iron.

q: In induced magnetism, the far end of the soft iron becomes a(n) _____.
e: Since the near end becomes an $S$-pole, the conservation of magnetic dipoles dictates that the far end must become an $N$-pole.
